summary: Modern Nashville country: 75-125 BPM, a live kit on a two-step or straight backbeat, a round bass on roots and fifths, strummed acoustic steel-string guitar, pedal steel and fiddle answering the vocal, I-IV-V with the II7; knowledge/style/country.json is its template
body: Tempo 75-125 BPM: ballads 70-85, mid-tempo 95-115, uptempo two-steps up to 125 and beyond.

Drums: a live acoustic kit played tastefully: kick on 1 and 3, snare (often a cross-stick in verses) on 2 and 4, the train-beat or two-step feel; modern country-pop may add programmed 808 kicks and claps.
Bass: a round electric bass on roots and fifths (root-five, a walk-up into the change), never busy.
Harmony: I-IV-V, I-V-vi-IV, and the country II7 (I-IV-II7-V7); strummed acoustic steel-string guitar as the bed, a telecaster and piano or organ on top.
Lead: pedal steel (sliding, swelling lines) and fiddle answering the vocal; in modern Nashville the steel sits lower and subtler.
Texture/master: polished but organic, vocal-forward, warm mids, natural room; no lofi or heavy distortion.

Sources (2026-11-26): Sound On Sound 'Nashville Recording'; iZotope '15 tips for mixing country music with Julian King'; Reverb 'How to get the Nashville sound in your home studio'; Splice 'Breaking down Nashville country music with Kate Malone and Devin Malone'; Produce Like A Pro 'Nashville pedal steel guitar recording'.

Apply: pattern/gmd-country-beat-1 on the drums, then pattern/prog-country-characteristic-3 on the keys four bars later. For a whole style change the Team Lead's restyle uses knowledge/style/country.json instead.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
